Zechariah 1:1: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:
Zechariah 1:2: “The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger.
Zechariah 1:3: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.
Zechariah 1:4: Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.
Zechariah 1:5: Your fathers—where are they? And the prophets—surely they will not live forever?
Zechariah 1:6: Yet receive My words and My ordinances, all that I, in My Spirit, command My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers.” And they answered and said, “As the Lord Almighty has arrayed Himself to act according to your ways and practices, so He acted toward you.”
Zechariah 1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month—which is the month Sabat—in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:
Zechariah 1:8: I saw in the night: look, a man mounted on a flame-red horse! He stood between the two shaded mountains, and behind him were flame-red, gray, dappled and white horses.
Zechariah 1:9: I said, “What are these, lord?” The angel speaking within me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
Zechariah 1:10: The man standing between the mountains answered and said to me, “These are the ones the Lord has sent out to travel around the earth.”
Zechariah 1:11: They answered the angel of the Lord standing between the mountains, “We have traveled around all the earth, and look, all the earth is inhabited and quiet.”
Zechariah 1:12: The angel of the Lord answered, “Lord Almighty, how long wilt Thou refuse mercy to Jerusalem and Judah’s cities, which Thou hast overlooked this seventieth year?”
Zechariah 1:13: The Lord Almighty answered the angel speaking within me with good words and comforting speeches.
Zechariah 1:14: The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,
Zechariah 1:15: and I am angry with great anger at the nations joining in assault, because I was a little angry, but they joined in attacking to bring evils.
Zechariah 1:16: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will again be extended over Jerusalem.”
Zechariah 1:17: The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities will again overflow with good things; the Lord will again have mercy on Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”
Zechariah 2:1: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, four horns!
Zechariah 2:2: I said to the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel.”
Zechariah 2:3: The Lord showed me four craftsmen.
Zechariah 2:4: I said, “What are these coming to do?” He said to me, “These horns that scattered Judah also shattered Israel, and none of them lifted a head. These entered to sharpen them for their hands—the four horns, the nations lifting a horn against the Lord’s land to scatter it.”
Zechariah 2:5: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, a man with a land-measuring cord in his hand!
Zechariah 2:6: I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long.”
Zechariah 2:7: Look, the angel speaking within me was standing, and another angel was going out to meet him,
Zechariah 2:8: and said to him, “Run and speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited fruitfully because of the multitude of people and animals within her.
Zechariah 2:9: I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”
Zechariah 2:10: “Oh! Oh! Flee from the northern land,” says the Lord, “because I will gather you from the four winds of heaven,” says the Lord.
Zechariah 2:11: Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!
Zechariah 2:12: For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.
Zechariah 2:13: Look, I am bringing My hand against them, and they will become spoils for those serving them; you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.”
Zechariah 2:14: “Delight and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell within you,” says the Lord.
Zechariah 2:15: Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
Zechariah 2:16: The Lord will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy land and again choose Jerusalem.
Zechariah 2:17: Let all flesh be reverent before the Lord, for He has risen from His holy clouds.
Zechariah 3:1: He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, with the slanderer standing at his right hand to oppose him.
Zechariah 3:2: The Lord said to the slanderer, “May the Lord rebuke you, slanderer! May the Lord, who chose Jerusalem, rebuke you! Look, is this not like a brand pulled from fire?”
Zechariah 3:3: Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and standing before the angel.
Zechariah 3:4: He answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” He said to him, “Look, I have taken away your lawless deeds; clothe him in a robe reaching to the feet,
Zechariah 3:5: and put a clean turban on his head.” They clothed him in garments and put a clean turban on his head, while the angel of the Lord stood by.
Zechariah 3:6: The angel of the Lord solemnly testified to Joshua, saying:
Zechariah 3:7: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: If you walk in My ways and keep My commands, you will govern My house. If you also guard My court, I will give you those who move about among these standing here.
Zechariah 3:8: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your neighbors sitting before you, for they are men who watch for portents. Look, I am bringing My servant, Rising.
Zechariah 3:9: For the stone I set before Joshua—on the one stone are seven eyes. Look, I am digging a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will feel out all the injustice of that land in one day.
Zechariah 3:10: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each of you will invite his neighbor beneath a vine and beneath a fig tree.”
Zechariah 4:1: The angel speaking within me returned and roused me as when someone is awakened from sleep,
Zechariah 4:2: and said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a lampstand entirely of gold, with its lamp-bowl above it, seven lamps upon it, and seven pouring channels for the lamps above it.
Zechariah 4:3: Two olive trees stand over it, one to the right of the lamp-bowl and one to the left.”
Zechariah 4:4: I asked the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?”
Zechariah 4:5: The angel speaking within me answered me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, lord.”
Zechariah 4:6: He answered me, “This is the Lord’s word to Zerubbabel: Not by great power or by strength, but by My Spirit, says the Lord Almighty.
Zechariah 4:7: Who are you, great mountain, before Zerubbabel, to set things straight? I will bring out the stone of inheritance—an equality of grace, its grace.”
Zechariah 4:8: The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Zechariah 4:9: “Zerubbabel’s hands laid this house’s foundation, and his hands will complete it. You will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
Zechariah 4:10: For who treated the small days with contempt? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. These seven are the Lord’s eyes, looking over all the earth.”
Zechariah 4:11: I answered him, “What are these two olive trees to the lampstand’s right and left?”
